quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume the passenger has ridden a motorcycle before.
Do not assume they have experience and explain everything to them.
Not let them ask questions.
Skip explanations since they are just a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not assume they have experience and explain everything to them.
questions.explanation: Your passenger needs to know how to stay safe. Always explain what to do before every ride. Do not assume they know anything about motorcycles.

questions.question: When it comes to motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Assume everything works correctly.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than on a car. Always check your motorcycle before each ride.

questions.question: If you are feeling tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up.
Ride faster.
Ride on the shoulder.
Stop and rest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride when you are tired. On long trips, take a rest break every two hours to avoid fatigue.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Only the front brake.
Only the rear brake.
Both brakes at the same time.
One brake at a time, never both together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when stopping. Both brakes work best when used at the same time.

questions.question: A way to lower the risk of a crash is to:

options.text: Signal your intentions to other drivers.
Not look ahead while riding.
Wear dark clothes.
Position your motorcycle where it is hard to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Help other drivers see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show what you are doing. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: Most motorcycles:

options.text: Have only a front brake.
Have only a rear brake.
Have a front brake and a rear brake.
Have three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a front brake and a rear brake.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket or pants, look for:

options.text: Leather material.
Polyester material.
Light material.
Dark colors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather material.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and long pants to cover your arms and legs. Leather provides the best protection when riding.

questions.question: Your body removes about ______ per hour.

options.text: One drink
Two drinks
Three drinks
Four drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: One drink
questions.explanation: The body can clear alcohol from about one drink per hour on average.

questions.question: During a pre-ride check, make sure:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes cause friction with the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake before every ride. The brake lever should feel firm and hold the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?

options.text: Dark-colored clothes
Synthetic material clothes
Reflective clothes
A leather jacket

questions.correctAnswerText: Reflective clothes
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective gear so other drivers can see you. This makes you more visible on the road.

questions.question: To reduce your risk of a crash, you should:

options.text: Ride within a foot of the vehicle in front of you.
Wear dark clothing.
Signal only when you feel like it.
Stay alert and be ready to act to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be ready to act to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: Stay visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake lights, and lane position to tell others what you are doing. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always scan the road ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than riding during the day because you can see other vehicles' lights better.
Harder than riding during the day because you cannot see as well.
Not allowed on highways.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than riding during the day because you cannot see as well.
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because visibility is poor. Without normal light and shadows, it is difficult to judge distances.

questions.question: The best gear to wear when you ride is:

options.text: Any gear that protects you.
The lowest-priced gear.
Gear that looks good.
Any gear that fits.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any gear that protects you.
questions.explanation: Wear gear that keeps you safe. A DOT-approved helmet is essential. Also wear face or eye protection and protective clothing.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, you should:

options.text: Decide if you can ride based on how you feel after drinking.
Set a limit beforehand so you can ride safely.
Not ride.
Not worry if you feel fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not ride.
questions.explanation: Do not ride after drinking. Even a small amount of alcohol can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle:

options.text: You can exceed the speed limit until the pass is done.
You can ignore "No passing" markings if you started passing in a legal zone.
You can pass on the shoulder.
You must stay within the speed limit and pass only in legal passing zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stay within the speed limit and pass only in legal passing zones.
questions.explanation: Only pass where it is safe and legal. Always obey the speed limit while passing.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: A jacket
Boots
Gloves
A stocking cap

questions.correctAnswerText: A stocking cap
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing that covers your arms and legs. Sturdy jackets, boots that support your ankles, and gloves are all important.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Do not have blind spots because they are small.
Have small blind spots that should not worry you.
Have blind spots you should check regularly.
Are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots you should check regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your routine.

questions.question: Motorcycle gloves are usually:

options.text: Made of leather.
Made of wool.
Not pre-curved.
Unsafe for riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Made of leather.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding boots should have soles that:

options.text: Are hard, durable, and slip-resistant.
Allow your feet to breathe.
Have tall heels.
Are soft and thin.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are hard, durable, and slip-resistant.
questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are sturdy and tall enough to support your ankles. Choose footwear with hard, durable, slip-resistant soles.

questions.question: What is often found in the center of the lane?

options.text: A landing strip
An oily or greasy strip
Lane markings
Ice

questions.correctAnswerText: An oily or greasy strip
questions.explanation: Oil and grease from cars drip and collect in the center of each lane. Unless the road is wet, a motorcycle can usually ride safely on this center area.

questions.question: Under Oregon law, what is required for a motorcycle's headlight?

options.text: It must only be on between 7 p.m. and 7 a.m.
It must be yellow in color.
It must be on whenever the motorcycle is being ridden.
The motorcycle may have four lights on the front.

questions.correctAnswerText: It must be on whenever the motorcycle is being ridden.
questions.explanation: Oregon law requires motorcycles to have their headlights on at all times while riding. Using your headlight helps other drivers see your motorcycle.

questions.question: What happens when you take a corner too fast?

options.text: You may drift into another lane.
It is better than going too slowly.
You will usually stay in your lane.
It is acceptable because motorcycles are smaller than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drift into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or go off the road. Slow down before turning or going around a curve.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your specific motorcycle?

options.text: The owner's manual.
A general book about motorcycles.
A previous owner.
Someone who knows about motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It contains details about how your motorcycle works, its features, and maintenance needs.

questions.question: What type of boots or shoes provide the best protection when riding?

options.text: Boots or shoes made of soft material.
Boots or shoes with long laces hanging loose.
Sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles.
Boots or shoes with tall heels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles.
questions.explanation: Choose tall, sturdy boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low to prevent catching on objects. Tuck in long laces so they don't get caught in the motorcycle.

questions.question: Should you use a turn signal when it is obvious you are turning?

options.text: No, you do not need to use a turn signal.
Yes, you should always use a turn signal.
Only if there are pedestrians nearby.
Only if you are at a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you should always use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: You must use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if it seems obvious. Always signal because other vehicles nearby may not see you, even if you think no one is around.
